beats.t: The stairs were longer than expected. With every step down, the rain sounded a little closer. It felt as though rain was falling even underground.
Rain in a basement. Who did this library's drainage? One star.
(Star ratings are my job. Moka's invading my territory.)
The door at the bottom opened by itself. The air inside was cold and clear, as though nobody had ever breathed it before.
Books as transparent as glass bottles hung in midair from red threads. Golden rules appeared on the floor.
[ Basement Level 3 · Things That Have Not Happened · Open a book, and it comes a little closer ]
Things that haven't happened are in books? Then is the whole future here?
Less the future than things that might happen. They might come to be, or never happen at all.
Wait. Hey, look. Moka's Solo Underground Show Sells Out. Can I open this?
It says opening it brings it a little closer. It doesn't say you can skip practice.
Then what's the point?! If a sold-out show gets closer but my skills stay the same, that's just humiliation getting closer.
Moka really doesn't practice his rap, huh.
I do! While you're asleep!
So that was the rhythm coming through the wall every night.
Beatboxing, not mice! Are those cat ears just decorations?
The baby dragon on Yeoni's wrist stretched its neck toward the rain. The water it had drunk earlier still sloshed inside its belly.
Want another drink? No. You'll burst. I'll really give you one star this time.
Smiling, Yundal moved toward the next shelf. His fingertips touched a thin book, then stopped.
[ Yundal Goes Home · 0 pages ]
Mister. Zero pages.
Con artist, did you really plan on never going back? Why isn't there even one line?
It has a cover. That's enough. Having a cover means it isn't over yet.
He withdrew his hand without touching the book again. Inside his glove, the hole made a tiny sound of wind.
Then I'll call your name every day. Yundal, Yundal. That'll make your book upstairs one page thicker every day, too.
A page a day means three thousand pages in ten years. That book will be too heavy to carry.
Don't worry. I'll carry it. Delivery fee charged separately.
Yundal smiled. This time, there wasn't a trace of teasing in it.
Meanwhile, Yeongnyangi walked ahead alone. Even at forks, he never hesitated. Like a route he'd taken many times.
Mr. Cat, do you know the way? Isn't this your first time here?
I'm following the smell. The wet pawprints go this way, too.
(The pawprints ended back on the stairs.)
Following Yeongnyangi, Yeoni noticed a book. Half the title on its pale pink cover was blurred.
[ Flower Pig · By the Cherry-Blossom River with the White □□ · 0 pages ]
White what? With a white what? Why is that the part that's blurred?!
White rice cake. For you, it's a white rice cake. A book about eating rice cakes by a cherry-blossom river.
Don't make me a glutton even in a book with zero pages!
Ahead, Yeongnyangi's tail stopped for the briefest instant, then swayed again. He did not turn.
In the deepest part stood a small pedestal with one book on it. Unlike the others, it was not transparent. Black cloth covered it, and black chains bound it.
White letters marked the cover. Flower Pig · The First Spring.
Found it. It was here.
One moment. Why is a book that's supposedly on loan here? And these are the shelves of things that haven't happened.
What does that mean?
It means a spring that happened somewhere has now become something that never happened. Someone hid this book here.
A padlock hung at the center of the chains. Two characters were engraved on it. 壬午.
Yeoni's heart thudded. The empty Year space on their chart seemed to pull toward those two characters.
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □辰 ]  5/8 — Response: 壬午
My Year Pillar. My characters are inside this book.
Yeoni touched the lock with a hoof. Instantly, the golden writing on the floor turned red.
[ Access denied · Flower Pig has already read one book (1/1) ]
Oh. The lullaby.
Then I'll open it. Move over.
When Moka grabbed the lock, the chains writhed like snakes and flung his paw away.
[ Access denied · Owner only ]
The owner can't open it, nobody else can open it. Then who can open this book?!
It's okay. I don't regret it. That little one will sleep well tonight.
Yeoni smiled. Yet the tips of their hooves trembled a little. Their spring was right before their eyes, beyond their reach.
Yeoni. Don't open that book. Don't look for a way, either.
His voice was strangely low. Yeoni slowly turned to look at Yeongnyangi.
You know this book.
I don't know, either. It's the first time I've seen it.
Liar. Your fur stands up when you lie. It's standing up now.
Yeongnyangi did not answer. Instead, he lifted his left paw a little. As Yeoni's voice sharpened, the scorch marks on it darkened.
When the card smelled of rain, when we saw the empty shelf—you were the only one acting strange. What is it? What are you hiding?
I can't tell you now. I'm sorry.
Now? Then when? With you, it's always later!
Hey, hey. Both of you, calm down. Fight after a meal. An empty stomach makes your words harsher.
Stay out of it, Moka. This is between us.
Yeoni's right. This is my problem.
You're both saying the same thing. That's why you're fighting.
Yeongnyangi's paw twitched again. Yeoni didn't see. They had already turned back toward the book.
You two. Wait a moment. The air has changed.
The shadow beneath the pedestal swelled. Black fingers rose through every gap in the chains and clutched the book.
The vessel's first spring. That was mine from the beginning.
You again? Stop eating other people's books!
Not eating, child. Taking back.
Dozens of black hands lunged at once. Yeongnyangi sprang forward, slashing his claws, and fire sparked from Moka's ladle.
Yundal took off his glove. With a rush of wind, the hole in his palm sucked in handfuls of black hands.
Urgh... Today's menu is rather salty.
The hole spread about a finger joint toward his wrist. Still smiling, Yundal raised the hand again.
Mister, stop! The hole's getting bigger!
It's all right. If it's to protect your book, my lady, I'll put this much on your tab.
Then real rain began falling from the ceiling. Between the black hands, a black shadow slid down the streams of rain.
The tiger. It leaped onto the pedestal and pressed a paw onto the book. The black hands withdrew as though recognizing a master.
Retrieving it. I'll take this.
Retrieving? That's my name on the book. Does your ledger even include other people's springs?
You're late. But very well. Bring it.
No!
Yeoni leaped up and grabbed the other side of the book. Over the chains, the pig's hoof and the tiger's paw touched.
It lasted only an instant. The tiger's paw trembled. A raindrop fell onto the top of Yeoni's head.
Why... are you smiling in the rain?
I don't know. Rain just makes me happy. It always has.
The tiger's red eyes shook. But the next moment, the ring at its neck flashed and tightened.
The tiger jerked the book away. The chains slipped from Yeoni's hooves.
Rain is just rain. There's nothing to be happy about.
Why are you taking that book? Were you in that spring, too? Is that why you erased the borrower's name?
So many questions. Debtors aren't supposed to ask questions.
I don't owe you anything!
Yes. Let it end that way this time. That's better for you.
With the book in its mouth, the tiger bounded up the stairs. Three or four steps at a time, leaving wet tracks, it vanished toward the domed ceiling.
After it! This time, I'm tying a ribbon on that striped tail.
Yundal sank down with his back against the pedestal. He cradled his ungloved hand against his chest.
Go ahead. I'll sit for a moment and follow. It would be nice if Mr. Otter stayed beside me.
Why me, of all people?
Because you're the loudest. Beside a loud person, I don't get forgotten.
That's cheating, con artist. Fine. But you owe me a meal later.
We're going together.
Okay. But when this is over, tell me everything. Promise.
When it's over.
Cat. Don't lose the pig. If you do, I'll shave off all your fur.
Never thought I'd live to be threatened by an otter.
Yeoni never asked whether that answer was a promise. Side by side, the two ran up the wet stairs.
Beyond the top of the stairs, the rain grew louder. Under the domed ceiling, the entire breathing library was slowly getting soaked.
[ The First Spring · On loan · Borrower: ■■■ ]
The three black squares on the borrowing card blurred little by little in the rain, as though a three-syllable name were about to rise from beneath them.
